1) It all depends on what you want. You may be better served buying a used bike at a local bike shop. I have found some good deals on bikes for under $200, but I'm also a very competent home mechanic.

An additional plus to buying from a local bike shop is that they can get the right size for you and adjust the bike to your liking.

2) Ride on bike trails and quiet streets as often as possible. I have been riding for over 35 years, and bike commuting for 20. Think of riding like any other acquired skill: The more you do it, the better you'll get.

My partner went from not having ridden a bike for 15 years to daily commuting in city traffic in roughly a year, but she rode at every possible opportunity. She can now thoroughly outpace me through city traffic, thanks to riding in rush hour daily.

3) Take it to a good mechanic. For roughly $50-$100, plus parts, you can ensure that everything is correctly adjusted and the bike is fit to you.

Many local bike shops will also have beginner's maintenance classes that are immensely helpful. You will learn how to change a tire, make quick adjustments, and perform routine maintenance to keep your bike rolling right and to keep you from getting stranded.

ETA: Get lights for your bike and always wear a helmet. Brain damage and tire tracks on your back are not pleasant...
